observations:
Torah #202 has zero bechina edges in torahData.js, and the source text contains no bechina language whatsoever. The teaching presents exactly one relationship: small intellect (שֵׂכֶל קָטָן / דַּעַת קַלָּה) causes a proportionally greater desire for honor (כָּבוֹד). This is a pure eitza relationship — causal, directional, inverse — not a bechina equivalence. The framework requires bechina-connected concepts (sharing the same essential nature, expressed with explicit bechina language) to form a package. Since there are no bechina relationships in this Torah at all, no package can be proposed.

The three conceptual elements in the text — שֵׂכֶל, דַּעַת, and כָּבוֹד — do not form a bechina cluster. The da'at↔sekhel apparent synonymy is contextual, not formally declared; and both are causally related to kavod (eitza), not essentially identical to it. Even if one were to propose that da'at and sekhel share the same essential nature in this Torah (which is arguable), this would yield only a 2-node bechina cluster between da'at and sekhel. A 2-node cluster of da'at↔sekhel is possible to propose as a package, but: (a) there is no explicit bechina declaration in the text to warrant it; (b) the usage is interchangeable-stylistic, not declarative; and (c) the more accurate reading is that both refer to the same faculty under different names, making them aliases rather than bechina-linked distinct concepts. No package can be honestly formed from this Torah's content.

The teaching's structure is a single causal axis with no branching, no mystical equation, and no parallel domains. There is no good package, no evil mirror package, and no neutral structural package. This Torah belongs to the category of practical-ethical aphorisms in Likutay Moharan (cf. Torah #198) that present behavioral/psychological observations without kabbalistic bechina structure.
